items.action: Replace the element selector `ds-combobox` with `ds-autocomplete`, in templates and in any stylesheet rule that names the element.
items.note: A rename to the industry word for the control. Behaviour is unchanged.

items.action: Replace `ComboboxComponent` with `AutocompleteComponent` in imports and references.
Replace `ComboboxOption` with `AutocompleteOption`, matching whole identifiers.
Replace `ComboboxSize` with `AutocompleteSize`.
Replace `--ds-combobox-focus-shadow` with `--ds-autocomplete-focus-shadow` - the only `--ds-combobox-*` hook at 0.4.0.
Update any hardcoded documentation link pointing at `#combobox` to `#autocomplete`.
items.appliesWhen: Only where a link to the docs site is written into your own code or README.
items.note: The docs page moved with the component rename, so the fragment that used to address it no longer resolves and the link lands at the top of the page.
items.verify: No documentation link in the consumer (code, README, a help panel) still points at the #combobox anchor.

items.action: Replace `ds-dropdown` with `ds-select` in templates and in any stylesheet rule that names the element, then apply `dropdown-error-input-rename` to the same elements. Set `placeholder="Select…"` where you relied on the dropdown's default (ds-select defaults to empty), and rename `--ds-dropdown-focus-shadow(-error)` to `--ds-select-focus-shadow(-error)`.
items.note: ds-dropdown is gone; ds-select is the one select-only picker, and it carries the CVA, invalid and hint, required and optional, per-option icons and readOnly.

items.action: On elements you moved from `ds-dropdown` to `ds-select`, rename `[error]` to `[invalid]` and `error="…"` to `invalid="…"`.
Replace `DropdownComponent` with `SelectComponent` in imports and references.
Replace `DropdownOption` with `SelectOption`, matching whole identifiers.
Replace `DropdownSize` with `SelectSize`.

items.action: Rename `.input` to `.search-input` in selectors scoped under `ds-search`.
items.appliesWhen: Only if you styled the undocumented inner class. Nothing in the public API moved.
items.pitfall: Scope the replace to selectors under ds-search. `.input` is generic enough that a repo-wide rename hits your own unrelated rules — the same leak this rename exists to stop.
items.note: The inner input class was over-generic, so a consumer global `.input` rule leaked into the component.

items.action: Look at every date picker. For the old click-only field pass `[allowInput]="false"`; to keep it full-width, set a width on the host.
items.pitfall: Two defaults moved at once and neither breaks a build: the field went from full-width to content-width, so a picker that used to fill its column now sits narrow inside it and the layout tuned around it has a hole.
items.note: The trigger is an editable masked text input by default (allowInput defaults to true) with a trailing calendar icon, and it sizes to its content.
items.restore: [allowInput]="false" for the click-only field, plus a width on the host to stretch it
items.verify: Every date picker either takes the editable masked trigger at content width, or says otherwise with [allowInput]="false" and a width.

items.action: If your readers are not en-US, set the locale: `[locale]` per instance, or `provideDsConfig({ datePicker: { locale } })` app-wide.
items.pitfall: The old display followed the ambient browser locale, so on your own machine nothing need look different while an en-GB or de reader sees a silently reformatted date. No markup changes and nothing logs.
items.note: The value display resolves `[locale] ?? provideDsConfig datePicker.locale ?? 'en-US'` instead of calling toLocaleDateString() with the browser default.
items.restore: [locale] per picker, or provideDsConfig({ datePicker: { locale: '<bcp47>' } })
items.verify: A screen whose readers are not en-US sets the locale rather than inheriting the new default.

items.action: To keep the old cap, set `--ds-search-maxw: 320px` on the host or in your theme. Move an override of the global `--search-maxw`, which is gone, to `--ds-search-maxw`.
items.note: The default max-width went from 320px to none, so ds-search stretches like the rest of the field family.
items.restore: --ds-search-maxw: 320px on the host or the theme
items.verify: Every search box is meant to stretch with its container, or pins the old 320px cap.

items.action: If you hand-rolled keyboard activation on an interactive card — a `(keydown.enter)` or `(keydown.space)` that fires the same action — delete it.
items.appliesWhen: Only cards carrying `elevation="interactive"`. Others are untouched, and so is anyone who never faked the keyboard path.
items.pitfall: Leaving the workaround makes the action fire TWICE on one key press, because the native activation runs beside it. A double submit or a double navigation is the symptom, and it shows only on the keyboard — a mouse test passes.
items.note: `elevation="interactive"` is natively keyboard-activatable now: Enter and Space trigger the click, with role="button" and a tabindex.
items.verify: No interactive card carries a hand-rolled keyboard activation beside the built-in one - two handlers on one card fire twice.

items.action: Build after upgrading, then rename your own member or mark it `override` wherever the compiler reports a collision with a class in `detect`. Delete an override of a member the class lost.
items.appliesWhen: Only a class that extends one of the classes in `detect`. A consumer who uses the elements in templates needs nothing from this item.
items.pitfall: `private` and `protected` give no protection: a member you redeclare collides with a base member of any visibility. A member of yours that replaced a lost one no longer replaces anything, and the component stops calling it.
items.note: `CardComponent` gained `interactive`. `ColorPickerComponent` and `MultiSelectComponent` each gained `ngOnDestroy`. `NumberStepperComponent` gained `ariaLabel`. `TabComponent` gained `value`. `ToastComponent` gained `isLoading`. `ToastService` gained `toastConfig`. `DrawerComponent` gained `ngOnDestroy` and `placement`. `AccordionComponent`, `AvatarComponent`, `CheckboxComponent`, `InputComponent`, `PopoverComponent` and `SidenavItemComponent` each gained 3. `AccordionItemComponent`, `BadgeComponent`, `BottomSheetComponent`, `ModalComponent`, `SelectComponent` and `TextareaComponent` each gained 4. `StepperComponent` gained 5. `TableComponent` gained 6. `RadioComponent` gained 7. `MenuItemComponent` gained 17. `DatePickerComponent` gained 46 and lost `displayLabel` and `trigger`. `SwitchComponent` gained 4 and lost `classes`. `TabsComponent` gained 10 and lost `selectedTemplate` and `tabsClasses`. `ToastRegionComponent` gained 5 and lost `entries`. `AutocompleteComponent` (the renamed `ComboboxComponent`) gained 11.
items.verify: The app builds with no error naming a class listed in `detect`, and every member of such a subclass that shares a base member's name is marked `override`.

informational: New ds-time-picker (24h/12h via provideDsConfig, range mode, CVA) — additive.

Selection controls gain size + required; standalone ds-radio gains invalid/hint; input/textarea maxLength counter; date-picker minDate/maxDate/disabledDate/presets + locale/dateFormat/firstDayOfWeek/defaultMonth manual masked entry; select clearable/icons/readOnly; autocomplete optionGroups/allowCreate/width=content; table expandable rows; modal closeOnBackdrop/persistent/xl/fullscreen; drawer placement/sm; bottom-sheet snapPoints; toast loading/promise/maxVisible; menu dividers/submenus; popover arrow/placement; tabs lazy/scrollable/closable/vertical; accordion single-open/item disabled; stepper clickable/errorSteps/vertical; sidenav collapsed tooltip; badge count/max; avatar status/fallbackIcon — all additive.

Public --ds-* customization token sweep across 47 existing components — purely additive resolvers, zero visual change when unset, except ds-search, whose max-width default moved from 320px (the removed global --search-maxw) to none through the new --ds-search-maxw (its own item).

Visual-only: rounded press feedback (+ --ds-press-brightness/--ds-press-scale tuning tokens) and native tap-highlight suppression; accessibility hardening across overlays/pickers/fields/cards (dialog semantics, Tab close, role=alert re-announce, labels).
